headline: Core splits contracts verified on Etherscan with public repo match, but auditors (Zach Obront independent + Nethermind) are not on the prompt's recognized-firm list; token and credential-NFT verification status not confirmed this run
short_headline: Verified splits; audit firm recognition gap

findings.text: ImmutableSplitControllerFactory (0x49e7) confirmed verified on Etherscan (abiSource: 'etherscan') via defipunkd surfacer. ImmutableSplitController (0xaF12) and ObolLidoSplit (0x2fB5) addresses are explicitly listed in the obol-splits GitHub README with matching Etherscan links, consistent with verified source. ObolValidatorManagerFactory (0x5754) listed in README as mainnet-deployed with Etherscan link. Token (0x0B01) and credential-NFT (0xfdb3) verification status could not be confirmed this run — defipunkd.com/api/contract/abi endpoint returned access-denied for those addresses.

GitHub repo ObolNetwork/obol-splits (https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-splits) confirmed public with all pinned address-book addresses (split 0x2fB5, factory 0x49e7, controller 0xaF12, withdrawal-recipient factory 0x5754) explicitly listed in the README. No specific deploy-commit SHA was pinned in this run; branch 'main' has 211 commits as of fetch. Repo README states 'Releases of this repo constitute post-fix review, audited commits.' No bytecode diff performed — recorded as scope limit.

Audit coverage confirmed from Obol security docs page: (1) Zach Obront independent researcher, Sept 18–22 2023, covering obol-splits Solidity contracts; (2) Nethermind Security V2 audit of obol-splits 2025; (3) Nethermind Security V3 audit of obol-splits 2025. Sigma Prime and Quantstamp audits cover Charon middleware only, not smart contracts. The 2025 Nethermind audits are recent and appear to cover current deployed versions. Audit PDFs are linked at https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-splits/blob/main/audit/.

Zach Obront is listed as an independent security researcher (not a named firm). Nethermind Security is a recognized security firm in the Ethereum ecosystem but does not appear in the prompt's explicit recognized-firm list (Trail of Bits, Zellic, Spearbit, OpenZeppelin, ConsenSys Diligence, Certora, Quantstamp, Halborn, Peckshield, Sigma Prime, ChainSecurity, Ackee Blockchain, MixBytes, Statemind). Per rubric V4, unknown or unlisted firms are orange-at-best for green-grade claims. Quantstamp (recognized) audited Charon middleware, not smart contracts.

Post-audit drift: repo has 211 commits on main with latest release v0.4 (Dec 2, 2025). Nethermind's V2 and V3 audits from 2025 appear to follow the 2023 Zach Obront audit and cover new contract versions. The README explicitly states releases constitute post-fix reviewed, audited commits. Specific diff content between audited commits and current deployed bytecode was not sampled this run — recorded as scope limit rather than downgrade signal.

The defipunkd surfacer for factory (0x49e7) shows no proxy — the contract is ImmutableSplitControllerFactory, a non-proxy contract. No proxy.implementation field was present in the surfacer response. The split-controller (0xaF12) also confirmed directly via factory's controller() return value. No proxied contracts detected among the contracts assessable this run; the token (0x0B01) proxy status is unknown.

steelman.red: The token (0x0B01) and credential-NFT (0xfdb3) verification status could not be confirmed, and neither Zach Obront (individual researcher) nor Nethermind (not on the prompt's recognized list) satisfies the strict recognized-firm requirement for green — leaving material audit-recognition and verification gaps.
steelman.orange: The core splits contracts (factory, controller, split) are verified on Etherscan and match the public obol-splits GitHub repo; recent 2025 Nethermind audits cover current deployed versions; however, Nethermind is absent from the prompt's recognized-firm enumeration and two contracts' verification status was unconfirmable this run, keeping the grade below green.
steelman.green: Nethermind Security is widely recognized in Ethereum security practice, the 2025 V2/V3 audits are recent and repo-linked, all assessed contracts appear source-verified on Etherscan, and the public repo maps every pinned address explicitly — a reasonable practitioner would call this green.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because the smart-contract auditors are Zach Obront (independent researcher, not a named firm) and Nethermind Security (not in the prompt's explicit recognized-firm list per V4), and the token (0x0B01) and credential-NFT (0xfdb3) bytecode verification status could not be confirmed this run. The core splits contracts are verified and the public repo matches, but the audit firm recognition gap and unconfirmed verification of two address-book entries prevent a green grade.

protocol_metadata.about: Obol builds Distributed Validator Technology (DVT) for Ethereum, enabling groups of node operators to collectively run a single Ethereum validator through threshold signing and distributed key generation. Users stake ETH via Obol's infrastructure which uses distributed validators to improve resilience, fault tolerance, and client diversity. The obol-splits contracts manage fee recipient and withdrawal address routing for DV clusters, splitting rewards among operators. The OBOL token serves as the coordination mechanism for the protocol's economic layer.
